short: Ce and Er Co-doped TiO2 for rapid bacteria-killing using vis
title: Ce and Er Co-doped TiO2 for rapid bacteria-killing using visible light

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: TiO2 photocatalysts harvest mainly UV light, so sunlight-driven rapid disinfection with TiO2 is weak. Er up-conversion of NIR to visible plus Ce narrowing the gap, both suppressing recombination, should boost visible-light bacteria killing by TiO2.
states.detail: Absorbed: b1 (HYP/need), b2 (HYP/hypothesis), b3 (DES/modification), b4 (DES/variable_sweep), b5 (PRC/synthesis), b8 (DES/down_select), b9 (DES/variable_sweep), b10 (PRC/synthesis)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Er and Ce are incorporated in the co-doped particles, Er as Er3+ and Ce as a surface Ce3+/Ce4+ mixture

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Visible absorption of Er-doped TiO2 (Er 4f lines at 488-654 nm) peaks at Er0.5Ti-O; band edge essentially unchanged. Er0.5Ti-O up-converts NIR excitation into green (520-570 nm) and red (640-690 nm) emission, stronger than Er0.75Ti-O.
states.detail: Absorbed: b6 (PRP/value), b7 (PRP/value), b13 (PRP/value), b15 (PRP/value), b16 (MEC/pathway), b17 (PRP/value), b18 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Lower PL intensity means slower electron-hole recombination and longer carrier lifetime; Smaller Nyquist arc = lower charge-transfer resistance; higher photocurrent = better carrier separation; A Ce3+/Ce4+ mixture on photocatalyst surfaces traps holes and electrons (refs 42, 48, 53); Better photocatalytic performance means more ROS and stronger antibacterial action (ref 54)

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Under simulated sunlight for 20 min, Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O kills ~91% of S. aureus and ~93% of E.

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Er-Ce co-doped TiO2 is driven by sunlight to fast visible-light photocatalytic sterilization, via Ce gap narrowing, Er up-conversion and suppressed recombination

nodes.title: EDS:spectrum, XPS:region, F5, F6
nodes.head: EDS spectrum shows Ti, O and a dominant C peak, with small Er (~1.4 keV) and Ce (~4.8 keV) peaks. XPS: Ti 2p3/2 458.5 and 2p1/2 464.2 eV; O 1s components 529.0, 531.2, 533.0 eV; Er 4d at 168.8 eV.
nodes.solves: Er and Ce are incorporated in the co-doped particles, Er as Er3+ and Ce as a surface Ce3+/Ce4+ mixture
nodes.note: Er peak barely above background text cites O 1s as Fig. 5(c) but it is panel b; crop caption spans are shifted by one panel
nodes.detail: o19: EDS spectrum shows Ti, O and a dominant C peak, with small Er (~1.4 keV) and Ce (~4.8 keV) peaks; o20: XPS: Ti 2p3/2 458.5 and 2p1/2 464.2 eV; O 1s components 529.0, 531.2, 533.0 eV; Er 4d at 168.8 eV; o21: Ce 3d region is noise with no resolved peaks at the marked u/v positions, and the Er 4d fitted envelope sits well above the noisy data

nodes.title: evidence, F2
nodes.head: Er-doped spectra show sharp absorption lines at ~488, 522, 545, 654 nm, absent for TiO2. Visible absorbance ranks Er0.5 > Er0.75 > Er1 > Er0.25 > TiO2 (522 nm line ~0.38 vs ~0.34, 0.20, 0.12)
nodes.solves: Visible absorption of Er-doped TiO2 (Er 4f lines at 488-654 nm) peaks at Er0.5Ti-O; band edge essentially unchanged
nodes.note: absorption edge stays near 400-410 nm for all; Er0.75 edge slightly blue
nodes.detail: o1: Er-doped spectra show sharp absorption lines at ~488, 522, 545, 654 nm, absent for TiO2; o2: Visible absorbance ranks Er0.5 > Er0.75 > Er1 > Er0.25 > TiO2 (522 nm line ~0.38 vs ~0.34, 0.20, 0.12)
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for b6 (o1, o2).

nodes.title: evidence, F3
nodes.head: Emission in 520-570 nm (a) and 520-570 plus 640-690 nm (b) is ~3x (a) and ~7x (b) stronger for Er0.5Ti-O than Er0.75Ti-O
nodes.solves: Er0.5Ti-O up-converts NIR excitation into green (520-570 nm) and red (640-690 nm) emission, stronger than Er0.75Ti-O
nodes.note: peak ~3.8e5 vs 1.3e5 (a), ~1.2e5 vs 1.8e4 (b); caption says 880 nm for (a), text says 808 nm
nodes.detail: o3: Emission in 520-570 nm (a) and 520-570 plus 640-690 nm (b) is ~3x (a) and ~7x (b) stronger for Er0.5Ti-O than Er0.75Ti-O
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for b7 (o3).

nodes.title: UVVIS:Tauc, F4
nodes.head: Co-doped absorption edges extend well past 420 nm into the visible vs a sharp TiO2 edge near 410 nm; Ce0.2 absorbs most. Tauc intercepts: TiO2 2.90, Er0.5Ce0.1 2.46, Er0.5Ce0.2 2.20, Er0.5Ce0.3 2.32 eV.
nodes.solves: Ce co-doping narrows the optical band gap of TiO2 from 2.90 eV to 2.20-2.46 eV, smallest (2.20 eV) at Ce 0.2
nodes.op: compare across conditions, fit model, overlay model on data
nodes.note: gap values rest on tail extrapolation; x axis unit not printed
nodes.detail: o5: Co-doped absorption edges extend well past 420 nm into the visible vs a sharp TiO2 edge near 410 nm; Ce0.2 absorbs most; o6: Tauc intercepts: TiO2 2.90, Er0.5Ce0.1 2.46, Er0.5Ce0.2 2.20, Er0.5Ce0.3 2.32 eV; o24: Doped-sample Tauc lines are drawn through the sub-edge tail (hv ~2.3-2.9) carrying the Er line near 2.37 eV, not the main edge near 3 eV
nodes.inner_audit: o24: gap values rest on tail extrapolation; x axis unit not printed

nodes.title: ECHEM:EIS, PL, F7, F9
nodes.head: PL band at 390-420 nm is strongest for TiO2, about half for Er0.5Ti-O and lowest for Er0.5Ce0.2. Nyquist plot: Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O shows a small arc (~1.5 kOhm) then a sloped tail; TiO2 rises almost vertically with no closed arc.
nodes.solves: Photogenerated electron-hole separation improves: recombination falls with Er and further with Ce, charge transfer resistance drops, photocurrent rises
nodes.note: legend reads 'Er0.5Ce0.2-O' (Ti missing); Ce-only control (Fig. S3) not in packet TiO2 arc is not resolved, so 'semicircle narrowed' is read only as a far larger TiO2 impedance dark current is ~40% of light current, not 'weak'; photo-response amplitude ~4e-6 vs ~2e-6
nodes.detail: o7: PL band at 390-420 nm is strongest for TiO2, about half for Er0.5Ti-O and lowest for Er0.5Ce0.2; o8: Nyquist plot: Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O shows a small arc (~1.5 kOhm) then a sloped tail; TiO2 rises almost vertically with no closed arc; o9: Light-on current ~7e-6 A/cm2 for Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O vs ~5.3e-6 for TiO2 over 8 on/off cycles; dark current ~3e-6 for both
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for b15 (o7).

nodes.title: evidence, F8
nodes.head: Degradation at 60 min: Er0.5Ce0.2 ~46% > Ce0.3 ~41% > Ce0.1 ~31% > TiO2 ~20%, same order at 20 and 40 min
nodes.solves: Photocatalytic dye degradation rises with co-doping, best for Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O (~46% vs ~20% for TiO2 in 60 min)
nodes.note: text writes MB for TiO2 and MO for the doped sample; caption says MO
nodes.detail: o10: Degradation at 60 min: Er0.5Ce0.2 ~46% > Ce0.3 ~41% > Ce0.1 ~31% > TiO2 ~20%, same order at 20 and 40 min

nodes.title: ASSAY, F10
nodes.head: Light: antibacterial ratio Er0.5Ce0.2 ~91% (c) and ~93% (d) > Ce0.3 ~87% > Ce0.1 ~68-73% > TiO2 ~45% > control ~4-7%. Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O light plates carry the fewest colonies for both strains; dark plates stay covered, sparser for doped samples
nodes.solves: Under simulated sunlight for 20 min, Er0.5Ce0.2Ti-O kills ~91% of S. aureus and ~93% of E. coli vs ~45% for TiO2
nodes.note: dark row: control and TiO2 plates densely covered (E. coli near-lawn); doped dark plates visibly sparser, consistent with the dark antibacterial ratios of F10c/d
